item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The entire GAW series of tales is a master class in characterisation—personalities of every character feel real and 3-dimensional, even in limited formats like chat logs. I honestly didn't completely understand what was going on with the actual anomalous abilities and entities encountered in some of the jude tales, but will admit I am on several benzodiazepines right now.

This tale caused some additional thoughts about my life and general experience, which may or may not be worth sharing.

+ show block
– hide block

I'm 27. I'm a trans woman. I was a near constant user of IRC chats between 2006 and 2011, and I've never really been able to use any real time chat client since then. Maybe it was just me or maybe the internet really did feel smaller back then, but the IRC channels I was part of were nothing like the ones depicted in GAW, except in tone and the constant use of memes; the reaction to the apparent suicide of a trans woman in the forum community the chat was associated with was along the lines of "1 down, 699,999 to go" and "all trannys should be killed". When I did out myself I encountered constant transphobia and misgendering in public channels alongside frequent sexual harassment in private messages; when I didn't, I saw it happen to other people. There were also tons of racial slurs, people saying "gas the jews" and "sieg heil o/", cis women being treated as sex objects, constant homophobia etc. I now know better places existed but at the time it didn't occur to me to look for them; I stayed with channels that were related to the very narrow set of interests I already had, and people who I trusted at the time (but shouldn't have) told me the rest of the internet was equally bad or worse.

From what I know—which is limited—things have changed, especially since ca 2014, when the communities I was part of took over huge swaths of the internet but also spurred women, people of colour and general non-fascists to unite and form visible and open communities against them. The only group chat I've been part of since then was a very small group of trans women, all of whom I alienated by being kkrule irl so that they eventually formed a new group chat without me, but during the time I did talk to them they were all part of various other online communities, all of which they reported as trans-friendly, women-friendly and lacking in racial slurs. But I still do find it hard to believe that there are any real time group chats that aren't grounded in, at very least, constant meanness towards those who don't fit in and forcing people to "grow a thicker skin" and so on, if not outright transphobia/racism/etc. So every time I see one of these chat logs where all the characters involved are not assholes it somewhat breaks immersion.

Reading articles like this, it's clear that people younger than me, and people who had other interests than me, had a very different experience. So the idea of an IRC chat (or local universe equivalent) where trans people are anything other than a community punching bag who get banned if they talk back… obviously doesn't break immersion for most people here. Which I guess is a sign of progress for the community?? Maybe I'm several years late on this, lol. To some extent the entire series has this escapist/wish fulfilment vibe, especially the chat portions, but maybe those are just accurate representations of life for gen z trans people online—I wouldn't know.

Apart from that, I guess I'm left unsure how to feel. The tale is undoubtedly a tragedy, but it loses some of that tragedy due to being set in a world of magic users. In real life there isn't a Jude who can turn up to coerce a trans person's family to accept them, or an anomalous island that can prevent the angry kid who caved a local III%er's head in from falling down the stairs onto some bullets in the local police station. (Or for that matter a power that can give a trans boy a body that's for all intents and purposes cis.) But I think the story expects us to realise that, and to understand how even more fucked all of these characters would be if the supernatural just ceased existing à la Quiet Days; unless I'm misreading it. I still do feel this blunts the tragedy, but the same is true of a lot of the foundationverse, aiming for horror or tragedy but failing because the reader knows real life is worse.

In any case I still think it's probably the most effective tale in the canon and has caused me to re-evaluate a lot of aspects of my life that I usually never think about. Maybe I just made some shitty decisions.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This was a really affecting read. I used to see GAW as interesting but not really serious, but now I'm astounded at the possible depth, humanity, and literature that could come from it. Having come from many years of internet chatting, it hit closer to home than might be expected; a lot of the characters remind me of the characters from my experiences in real life.

In particular, I was impressed by change of tone in Bones' measured, eloquent responses, and the utter humanity of the internet edgelord after they've made a serious mistake. Overall, it was refreshing and intriguing to see the "serious" side of GAWers — after all, they're just people, despite all the surreal/ironic memeing. Excellent job.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This works well - it's a very effective piece in terms of emotional manipulation (especially that last section, which was a very clever way to end) and character development. Heartily upvoted - it's one of my favourite GAW pieces.

I take Deci's point about it feeling a little rushed. PIC went from angry to murderer to forgiven a little too fast, and it would have had more impact if the death was a character we already knew. It's also a little convenient to give the Nazi a gun - it comes across as an attempt by the author to justify the actions of the characters, instead of leaning into their flaws and (im)moral choices, which might be more interesting. I would be very keen to read more about both Dove's character and PIC's actions in future works.

item.content:encoded: I'll put what I said in Discord on here as well. Everything breezes by too fast, so it gives it this odd feeling of… rushedness. The final section helps thematically and it was good to add it, but when everything hits their beats really quickly, it still feels like it just doesn't stop to consider its own story. So you have a good story that goes by too fast, making it less impactful than it could have been otherwise. If people like it as-is then people like it as-is. But there's just not enough time in the reading of the story to really let it hit me. It still can stand to be improved to allow readers more time to truly take in the impact this has, and just how serious it is for other members of GAW.
